newsitem.title: NORWAY: SAGA RESTARTS SNORRE OIL, VIGDIS STAYS SHUT IN.
newsitem.headline: SAGA RESTARTS SNORRE OIL, VIGDIS STAYS SHUT IN.

text.p: Saga Petroleum ASA said on Tuesday it had restarted oil output at the 200,000 barrels per day (bpd) North Sea Snorre field, which had been closed since Monday morning due to a problem in the production system.
Separately, the company said crude throughput at the 40,000 bpd Vigdis development remained shut in due to renewed problems with the gas compressor system.
Vigdis pipes crude to Snorre for processing before it is transported to the Gullfaks A platform for further processing, storage and loading.
Saga spokesman Bjoern Schibevaag said Snorre resumed oil production at 9.50 a.m (0750 GMT), having been halted since 4.20 a.m. (0220 GMT) on Monday.
"We should be back to normal production levels very soon," he said.

Snorre suffered a five-day unscheduled outage in July after a short circuit caused a power blackout and subsequent problems with the auxilliary generating system. Both systems must before functioning before oil production is permitted to restart.
Vigdis, which came on stream in January five months ahead of schedule, has had a series of production stoppages since April, linked to a design fault in the gas compressor system.
After the the latest incident the field resumed pumping on August 5. Due to Norwegian regulations governing gas flaring the compressor must be functioning before production can go ahead.
"We have had another failure in the same gas seal as before," Schibevaag said. "We are working on a new gas seal and we hope to have it in place and tested before August 25."
Vigdis is scheduled to go into maintenance on August 25 to coincide with a turnaround planned on the Gullfaks A platform.
Schibevaag said the company was looking at other options and possibilities for resuming output earlier, but he declined to give details.
